newsitem.title: RWANDA: Two more Rwanda genocide trials start.
newsitem.headline: Two more Rwanda genocide trials start.

text.p: The trials of two more people accused of participation in the slaughter of more than 800,000 people in Rwanda in 1994 started in the western border town of Gisenyi on Wednesday, state Radio Rwanda reported on Thursday.
"Callixte Ngendahimana and Javan Bavugayabuca went on trial yesterday for crimes committed during the genocide," the radio said, adding that prosecutors called for a death sentence.
The radio said the trials were adjourned to January 21.
Under Rwanda's 1996 genocide law those convicted have 15 days to lodge an appeal and the Appeals' court must hear the cases within three months.
The trials of four other men due in Nyamata, 35 km (21 miles) southeast of the capital Kigali, were postponed on Wednesday without explanation, court officials in the town said.
Some 37 suspects have so far been scheduled to stand trial in Kigali, Byumba, Gikongoro, Kibuye, Nyamata and Kibungo.
Two have been sentenced to death. The two, Egide Gatanaze and Deogratias Bizimana, told Reuters on Wednesday from their isolation cell in Kibungo prison that they had appealed.
Of the 35 remaining, 14 have made court appearances.
The scheduling of trials is still erratic as the tiny central African country struggles to rebuild its justice system after the 1994 state-sponsored slaughter.
